What you meet when it is on
Where each thing lives — no user table
The client secret — A or B

annotations.text:
DO YOU NEED A USER DATABASE?

No — not for a gate.

Keycloak already holds who people are, their password, their MFA and their leavers. A user table in roadmap.db would be a second, staler copy of a directory you do not own.

What OIDC actually needs stored:
- Settings (issuer, client id, claim name, allowlist) — one row in SQLite.
- Secrets (client secret, session signing key) — environment, never the database.
- The person — a signed cookie in the browser, holding sub and preferred_username. Not persisted.

A user table only becomes necessary when data belongs to a person: created_by, assignee, per-user preferences, an audit trail. Mastermind has none of those, and the brief forbids them.

See the Storage artboard below.

THIS IS DRAWN, NOT AGREED

CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 7 forbids accounts/roles/permissions and external integrations. Keycloak SSO is both.

The design here is the narrowest reading that could survive: a GATE. One allowlist, no roles, no user rows, nothing attributed to a person.

What would break the rule outright, and is deliberately absent: role-to-permission mapping, per-user views, an audit log, ownership on a project.

Nothing is built until you say which reading you want.

THE LOCK-OUT PROBLEM

A localhost tool that gates itself on a remote identity provider can be made unreachable by a typo, an expired secret, a VPN drop or the realm being reconfigured by someone else.

So the escape hatch is drawn on three artboards, not hidden in a runbook: MASTERMIND_SSO=off at startup skips the gate.

That env var is also what the test suite sets — 342 tests go through TestClient and must never reach a real realm.

WHY THE REDIRECT URI ROW FAILS BY DEFAULT

It is drawn failing because this is the step that fails in real life: Keycloak compares redirect URIs as exact strings, and http://localhost:8000 is not http://127.0.0.1:8000.

The app already serves on 127.0.0.1 per its own run command, so the panel offers both ways out — send the URI on, or move the app to localhost.

The copy button matters more than it looks: retyping a URI by hand into an admin console is how this goes wrong twice.
